name: Let LRMs Break Free from Overthinking via Self-Braking Tuning
authors: Haoran Zhao, Yuchen Yan, Yongliang Shen et al. (lead affiliation: Zhejiang University, ZJU-REAL; with Tianjin University and Microsoft Research Asia)
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv preprint 2505.14604, submitted May 2025; camera-ready Oct 2025)
reflection_type: learned-critic-model (the LRM is trained, via SFT on curated adaptive-length data, to internalize a self-regulating 'braking' behavior that recognizes when reasoning has become redundant and terminates it; reflection is over the model's own chain of thought rather than via an external critic)
feedback_source: ground-truth-oracle (overthinking is identified offline using the reasoning efficiency ratio measured against standard/correct answers — the position of the first correct answer in the trajectory — plus a curated lexicon of overthinking marker terms; this oracle signal is used only during training-data construction, not at inference)
iteration_structure: single-shot (at inference the SBT-tuned model produces one reasoning trajectory and autonomously stops; the data-construction pipeline analyzes existing OpenR1-Math trajectories step-by-step offline, but the deployed model is single-pass with no test-time iteration/retry)
reflection_object: reasoning chain (the chain-of-thought is the object: SBT prunes redundant Evolution Solutions from the reasoning trajectory and inserts metacognitive 'braking'/epiphany sentences); the learning is ultimately written into model weights via SFT, so it also modifies model weights
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update (SBT is supervised fine-tuning on the SBT-E / SBT-D adaptive-length datasets, i.e. the self-regulation behavior is baked into model weights; no in-context-only mechanism)
requires_training: SFT (supervised fine-tuning on OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D, each 92,064 examples, with loss masking on the retained redundant 'braking' segment)
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward used offline for data labeling (overthinking is detected with a verifiable, standard-answer-based reasoning efficiency ratio plus an overthink-marker lexicon, combined into an overthink score with weight beta=0.1); no online reward model or RL critic is used during training
distillation_target: model-weights (the self-braking behavior is distilled into the LRM's weights via SFT); the intermediate reusable artifacts are the two released training datasets OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D, each ~92K adaptive-length trajectories
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered training-data signal that induces emergent inference behavior: the truncation rule, overthink metrics, masking, and natural-language braking prompts are engineered, but after SFT the model spontaneously generates epiphany sentences (e.g. 'Wait, I've verified my answer. No need to continue thinking.') and terminates without external signals (~50% early-termination rate on AIME), an emergent self-regulation behavior
memory_type: none (no external memory store; the regulation is parametric — internalized in weights — not stored as episodic memory or a skill library)
memory_persistence: cross-task (the learned braking behavior is permanently in the fine-tuned weights and applies across all subsequent math-reasoning queries); not a runtime memory mechanism
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no runtime memory to curate; the analogous offline 'curation' is the SBT data-construction pipeline that prunes redundant Evolution Solutions and applies loss masking to a small retained 'braking' segment so overthinking is exposed but not reinforced)
error_localization_granularity: step-level (overthinking is detected at the level of reasoning steps/solutions — the transition from the Foundation Solution to redundant Evolution Solutions; SBT-D recomputes the overthink score after each step. The paper explicitly shows step-level detection beats token-level: AIME 14.17% vs 11.34% accuracy with fewer tokens)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (the braking corrects/truncates reasoning within a single problem-solving trajectory; there is no cross-task experience transfer or episodic carryover — the only cross-task element is that the behavior generalizes once trained into weights)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery (the model learns to detect overthinking in-flight and terminate the redundant portion of the current reasoning chain at an appropriate braking point, rather than retrying in a future episode)
benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, AMC23, AIME (AIME24 + AIME25); base/backbone models DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (analysis), Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
headline_result: Reduces token consumption by 30%-60% (up to ~62.8%) while preserving comparable accuracy. E.g. Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct: SBT-E cuts tokens 30.7% with only 2.65% accuracy drop, SBT-D cuts 23.0% with 1.95% drop; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: SBT-E cuts tokens 62.8% while preserving 94.1% of baseline accuracy. SBT-E averages 48.3% token reduction across models, SBT-D 43.9%.
baselines: Models SFT'd on the unmodified OpenR1-Math dataset (same 92K instances, 16K context, no SBT truncation) serving as the unconstrained baseline; internal ablations vs token-level detection, vs special-token guidance, vs no-guidance, and vs removing the Masked Redundant Thinking (MRT) segment
gains_vs_baseline: Versus the OpenR1-Math SFT baseline, SBT achieves 30%-60% fewer inference tokens with minimal accuracy loss. Best SBT-E config (threshold 0.2, beta 0.1, preserve 2 solutions + mask a few sentences) reaches 57.83% average accuracy at 1673 tokens vs baseline 59.36% accuracy at 3277 tokens — i.e. ~49% fewer tokens while retaining 97.4% of baseline accuracy. SBT-D can even improve MATH500 accuracy on Llama-3.1-8B by +2.62% while cutting tokens 58.7%.
compute_cost_profile: Inference token cost reduced 0.4x-0.7x of baseline (30%-60% reduction; up to 62.8%); fewer generated tokens per query. Training cost: one round of SFT on ~92K examples per dataset (SBT-E or SBT-D), comparable to ordinary SFT — no RL rollouts or reward-model training. Data construction is an offline pass over OpenR1-Math trajectories.
known_limitations: (1) Domain generalization: validated only on math reasoning; applicability to open-ended, commonsense, logical, or multimodal reasoning is unverified. (2) Data scalability/adaptivity: experiments limited to ~92K examples; scaling to millions untested; SBT-E/D rely on fixed thresholds that may need manual tuning per task. (3) Overthinking-signal definition: efficiency ratio + marker ratio may miss subtle/latent reasoning utility (seemingly redundant steps may serve hidden organizing purposes). (4) Interpretability/controllability: the internal termination decision remains opaque, with no explicit trace/control mechanism. (5) Complex-task trade-offs: for deep multi-step tasks (e.g. theorem proving) premature termination risks omitting critical steps.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: oracle-label/ground-truth (the overthinking-identification pipeline that builds the training data depends on standard/correct answers to compute the reasoning efficiency ratio — i.e. ground-truth labels are needed to locate braking points during data construction). However, the deployed model performs intrinsic-only self-braking at inference with no external feedback, tools, or oracle.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / net-positive for efficiency (consistently cuts tokens 30-60% with comparable or near-equal accuracy on math; SBT-D occasionally improves accuracy by removing harmful overthinking, e.g. +2.62% on MATH500 for Llama-3.1-8B). Math-specialized models gain less (more efficient already); general-purpose models gain more. Note the 'self-correction' here is redundancy-removal, validated against ground-truth during data construction.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper reports accuracy and token counts but does not directly measure confidence calibration / overconfidence; it argues a large fraction of LRM reasoning is genuinely redundant and removable without accuracy loss, but provides no calibration analysis)
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step (the overthinking-identification framework localizes where in the reasoning trajectory the model transitions from effective reasoning — Foundation Solution plus useful Evolution Solutions — to redundant computation, i.e. pinpoints the redundant steps; it does not build a general failure taxonomy or attribute across agents)
failure_mode_addressed: overthinking / redundant reasoning in large reasoning models (LRMs generate excessive Evolution Solutions and continue reasoning long after deriving the correct answer); cross-links to MAST-style 'overthinking' and to the broader 'reasoning tax' / redundant self-reflection failure mode. Does not target underthinking or premature termination (it explicitly guards against cutting too early via masking and preserving 2 solutions).
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — two SFT datasets released: OpenR1-Math-SBT-E and OpenR1-Math-SBT-D (each 92,064 adaptive-reasoning-length examples), plus code and trained self-braking models via the GitHub repo (ZJU-REAL/Self-Braking-Tuning) and project page
builds_on: DeepSeek-R1 / OpenAI o1-style large reasoning models; the OpenR1-Math reasoning-trajectory dataset (HuggingFace Open-R1); Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct and Llama-3 instruct backbones; the broader overthinking-mitigation literature it categorizes (RL length-reward methods, variable-length-CoT SFT, LightThinker, DEER, NoThinking, Token-Budget, Chain-of-Draft (CoD))
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by ~20 follow-up works in the efficient-reasoning / overthinking-mitigation line (e.g. surveys on efficient reasoning and length-controllable / adaptive-thinking LRM methods). Specific named successors are not individually confirmed from the fetched sources, so the precise list is [uncertain] beyond the aggregate citation set.
citation_count: 20 (Semantic Scholar, CorpusId 278769932, as of mid-2025; referenceCount 50)
reasoning_model_native: yes (the method specifically targets R1/o1-style large reasoning models with built-in long-CoT reflection; it is built on and evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-Distill and reasoning-tuned Qwen/Llama models, and addresses the overthinking that is native to such reasoning models)
on_policy_distillation_link: Related but distinct: SBT is offline SFT on curated adaptive-length trajectories derived from a stronger reasoning model's outputs (OpenR1-Math, i.e. DeepSeek-R1 distillation data) with overthinking pruned — it is a length/skill-optimization via static-data distillation rather than on-policy distillation; no on-policy sampling or online teacher is used.
sample_efficiency: Single SFT pass on ~92,064 curated examples per variant (SBT-E or SBT-D) suffices to induce the self-braking behavior; no iterative/multi-trial optimization. Best operating point identified at overthinking threshold 0.2 (labels ~60% of samples as overthinking), beta=0.1, preserving 2 solutions plus a small masked braking segment.
